prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor corner layout across the five frames as the camera wearer turns right from a wall with a mirror (frame 1) toward a multi-pane window and foreground clothing rack (frames 2–3), then pans back left toward a corner with a mannequin and small pedestal (frames 4–5). In frames 2 and 3, the bright horizontal bar and garments of the clothing rack lie within arm's reach in the lower-right foreground (~0.5–1.0 m), while the mannequin stands ~1.0–1.5 m away on the far-left edge in frames 2 and 4 (partially cut off by the frame boundary) and on the right in frame 5 (~1.2–1.5 m away, ~0.6 m right of the white display stand at ~1.5 m). In frame 5, the mannequin faces directly toward the camera wearer while a very bright region in the lower-right foreground (~0.2–0.4 m, within immediate reach) shows the camera wearer's right hand holding fabric that partially occludes the mannequin's lower torso. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB frames, the depth map more clearly separates the near clothing rack, foreground hand, and window Mullion grid from the background. However, the map is unreliable on reflective and transparent surfaces: it renders the flat mirror in frame 1 as a dark ~2–3 m recess behind the wall plane, and it inconsistently estimates the window glass as infinitely far (black) in frames 2 and 4 but as a flat mid-depth surface (~1.5–2.0 m) in frame 3.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map tracks discrete foreground figures across the camera wearer's pan-right-and-back-left motion, isolating a silhouette in the lower-left mirror in frame 1 (~2–3 m virtual distance, facing the viewer), a figure on the left edge in frame 2 (~1.0–1.5 m, partially out of view to the left), and two overlapping foreground/mid-ground masks on the right in frame 5. In frame 5, an upper pink mask outlines the front-facing mannequin at ~1.2–1.5 m while a lower brown mask (~0.2–0.4 m, within arm's reach at the bottom right) captures the camera wearer's right hand and held cloth occluding the mannequin's waist and hips. This instance separation in frame 5 makes the occlusion boundary between the held dark fabric and the dark-clothed mannequin behind it much clearer than in the RGB image alone. However, the map is highly unreliable in its semantic labels and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the inanimate mannequin as a 'person' in frames 2 and 5, merges the camera wearer's hand and held garment into a second 'person' mask in frame 5, and completely misses the mannequin during the blurred pan in frame 4. It also hallucinates large background masks over the window panes and outdoor trees, mislabelling them as a 'bus' in frame 2 and a 'tv' in frame 3 while failing to segment the foreground clothing rack (~0.5–1.0 m) or the left display stand (~1.5 m) in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1 through 4 as the camera pans past the mirror and window, detecting skeletons only in frame 5 on the right side of the scene when the view stabilizes on the corner. In frame 5, a yellow upper-body skeleton with symmetric shoulders, elbows hanging down, and clustered facial keypoints indicates a figure at ~1.2–1.5 m standing upright and facing directly toward the camera wearer, with its lower body cut off below the hips. At the bottom right of frame 5, within arm's reach (~0.2–0.4 m) and directly in front of the yellow torso's waist, magenta hand skeletons capture the articulated fingers of the camera wearer's right hand holding an item. While the keypoints clearly highlight the front-facing head orientation of the mid-ground figure and the fine finger placement of the foreground hand better than the low-contrast RGB regions, the map is spatially unreliable in several ways. It falsely assigns a human body skeleton to an inanimate retail mannequin, misses the mannequin in frames 2 and 4 as well as the mirror reflection in frame 1, and erroneously links the camera wearer's near-field hand keypoints (~0.3 m) to the mannequin's mid-ground wrists (~1.3 m) across a ~1 m depth gap.
